feature: Command E never flattens a recording
summary: Merge Down never takes a clip, a sound or anything with an in and an out, so Command E with a title picked over a recording no longer bakes the video into a still. Two still layers on a picture merge exactly as before.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/command-e-on-a-video-keeps-the-clip-walk.json.

try.do: Open the sample recording from the Welcome window.
Press T, click on the picture and type Shipping today, then press Command Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: With the title still picked, press Command E.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Open the Layer menu and look at Merge Down: it is dimmed.
On a picture, draw two shapes, pick the top one and press Command E: they merge into one picture as before.

evaluate: After Command E, are the recording and the title both still on the timeline with all their time?
Is a dimmed Merge Down with no message enough, or do you want a short note on the canvas saying why nothing happened?
Is Shift Command E for Export easy enough to find on a video, given Final Cut uses Command E?
rough: The mock prints Command E for Export MP4. Photoshop gives Command E to Merge Down and Premiere gives it to Edit Original (Premiere's Export is Command M), so neither tool gives it to Export: Command E stays Merge Down on a video and Export stays on Shift Command E (UX-PATTERNS §7).
Command E on a clip does nothing and says nothing: the row is dimmed, with no canvas note explaining why.
Premiere's Export key, Command M, is not added: on a Mac it is Minimize, and the task did not ask for it.
